check.reason: The target is pharma marketing and the cost it passes on to the system. Patients are not mocked, and the closing line about everyone else getting the invoice sides with them. It names no private individual, does not mock the reporter, and quotes nothing. It adds no invented numbers or results, and its claims stay within the summary (inappropriate prescribing, likely higher costs). The deadpan 'return on investment' and 'free lunch program' framing is satirical and does not misstate the story. It involves no death, children or violence.

pick.title: Pharma’s free lunches for doctors boost inappropriate prescribing, analysis finds
pick.headline: Drugmakers' Free Lunch Program Delivers Strong Returns, Analysis Finds
pick.take: A new review finds industry gifts and payments increased inappropriate prescribing, likely raising costs. Pharma has long treated the catered sandwich as purely educational, but the marketing budget clearly tracks its return on investment. The lunch was free only to the person eating it. Everyone else gets the invoice, itemized as premiums.
